inputs.root_cause: Both IPYNB-ID-001 obligations cited only cell-NAME uniqueness tests (test_duplicate_cell_names_are_rejected_from_4_2_onward etc.) -- a different capability (IPYNB-CELLNAME-001/CELLNAMEUNIQUE-001 territory) -- as their sole evidence. tests/python/ipynb/test_obligation_cell_identity.py's own docstring explicitly states it covers 'IPYNB-ID-001 (4.5): ids required, unique, charset and length constrained; generated ONLY via explicit upgrade, with a rewrite map', and contains a dedicated, complete, already-passing test block for exactly that (lines 185-257: test_duplicate_cell_ids_are_rejected, test_invalid_cell_ids_are_rejected, test_valid_cell_ids_are_accepted, test_ids_are_not_generated_by_a_passive_read, test_explicit_upgrade_generates_ids_and_reports_the_rewrite_map, test_upgrade_is_deterministic_for_identical_input, test_upgraded_notebook_validates_at_4_5) that was simply never cross-referenced into the evidence row. This is the same misattributed-evidence defect class found in XLIFF-STATE-001 (Event 103), now found a second time.

execution_steps: 1. Read SAL-IPYNB-00014 and the two obligations' rule_text directly before searching for evidence: 'Validate required cell IDs (uniqueness, syntax, length); generate IDs only via explicit upgrade with a rewrite map for references' and the nbformat 4.5 core rule (unique id, permitted charset/length, required since 4.5).

2. Confirmed the shipped namespace already implements this completely: codec/reader/reader.py's CELL_ID_PATTERN (charset+length) and a single unified check (missing/invalid-syntax/duplicate, IPYNB_CELL_ID) enforced in strict mode for minor>=5; model/lifecycle.py's upgrade() generates ids only there, reporting an id_rewrites list (cell_index, old_id, new_id) -- exactly the 'rewrite map' the rule_text names.

3. Grepped for existing shipped-namespace test coverage before writing anything new: test_obligation_cell_identity.py's own docstring already claims IPYNB-ID-001 coverage explicitly, and contains a complete, dedicated block (7 test functions, 16 parametrized cases) proving every element of the rule: duplicate rejection, 6 invalid-syntax/length negative cases, 5 valid-syntax positive cases including the exact 64-character boundary, passive-read never generates an id, explicit upgrade generates unique valid ids, upgrade is deterministic, and the upgraded notebook validates. Independently re-ran all 16 before citing them: all pass.

4. Also found test_obligation_lifecycle_modes.py::test_explicit_upgrade_is_the_only_production_path_that_generates_ids, which additionally cross-checks the upgraded document against nbformat.validate() -- nbformat is the official Jupyter Project reference implementation, already declared as this package's independent oracle (controller-state.yaml's ipynb_checkpoint: 'oracle: nbformat 5.10.4'). This is genuine independent-reference backing for the 'upgrade produces an officially valid notebook' claim specifically -- stronger than the SELF-CONSISTENT label this session used for nrrd/xliff promotions that had no such oracle. The duplicate/invalid-id rejection logic itself is format_factory's own check, not independently cross-verified against nbformat's own behavior for those specific inputs, so the promotion's truth_boundary distinguishes the two rather than blanket-claiming oracle backing for everything.
5. No new source or test code was needed -- corrected the evidence citation to the tests that already existed and already passed, and added no new assertions.
6. Re-ran the full ipynb suite to confirm no incidental regressions from touching only the evidence YAML: 670 passed (unchanged from Event 100's baseline).
